subject: humanities
passage: Katajjaq is a traditional vocal game of the Inuit of northern Canada. Two women stand face to face, often very close together, and take turns making quick, rhythmic sounds from the throat and chest. One singer sets a pattern, and the other answers with a different sound that fits around it. The game usually ends when one woman runs out of breath or starts to laugh, and the other is declared the winner.
stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To argue that katajjaq is more difficult than any other kind of singing
choices.B: To describe how a traditional Inuit vocal game is performed
choices.C: To explain how the Inuit first learned to make sounds from the throat
choices.D: To show that katajjaq singers rarely enjoy taking part in the game

explanation.why: After naming katajjaq as "a traditional vocal game," every sentence explains a part of how it is played: how the two women stand, how they take turns, and how the game ends. So the main purpose is to describe how the game is performed.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The text never compares katajjaq with other kinds of singing.
explanation.B: Correct. The text explains who takes part, how they trade sounds, and how a winner is decided.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text describes the game as it is played; it says nothing about how throat sounds were first learned.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The game can end when a singer "starts to laugh," which suggests fun, not a lack of enjoyment.
